criteria.reason: Both plans split the lesson cleanly along the same natural boundary (acquiring stability first, losing the post second), keep proper teaching order, and write one clear verb-first Brazilian Portuguese skill per lesson with a canonical topic, concrete example, and real-life use case.

A gives the writer a stronger, smoother plan with concrete dates in Lesson 1's worked example and follow-up check, clear continuity from Lesson 2's hook to its first explanation, and practice for every taught rule. B defines effective service circularly, jumps abruptly from a budget-limit hook to court rulings in Lesson 2, leaves the motivated-act rule unpracticed, and asks a flawed question in Lesson 2's application that implies budget-limit dismissals require a court sentence.

Both plans properly avoid unnecessary pictures and activities for a text-based legal topic, and B's Lesson 1 application table is reasonable, but B's Lesson 2 application sets visualKind to table for two non-parallel narrative scenarios that do not share comparable columns. A stays cleanly text-only throughout.

A explains legal terms in everyday language suited to beginners and grounds examples in concrete Brazilian public bodies (prefeitura, secretaria, autarquia, município, hospital público), despite a minor punctuation slip using guillemets. B uses stiffer legal jargon for beginners and relies only on generic terms like órgão and setor de pessoal.

observations.claim: In Lesson 1, the trap of thinking three years alone gives stability is planned only in the ungraded guess (screen 3), whereas the post-teaching checks test counting from the appointment date (screen 7) and having approval without completing three years (screen 8).
observations.learnerCost: Learners are not explicitly checked after instruction on the main misconception that completing three years alone grants stability.

observations.claim: Uses European Portuguese guillemets instead of Brazilian quotation marks in Lesson 1 screen 3 and Lesson 2 screen 3 (along with the phrasing 'Tem de aguardar').
observations.learnerCost: The punctuation looks slightly foreign to Brazilian readers if the writer copies it directly.

observations.claim: In Lesson 1, the trap of thinking three years alone grants stability appears only in the ungraded guess (screen 3) rather than in a post-teaching check (screen 8 tests approval without three years), and the guess option 'Também exige avaliação por comissão' introduces specific legal phrasing that can tip off the right answer before teaching.
observations.learnerCost: Learners can spot the correct guess from its specific legal wording and never face a post-teaching check on the time-alone trap.

observations.claim: Screen 5 defines 'efetivo exercício' circularly ('exercício funcional contado para essa finalidade') instead of in plain words, and the worked example on screen 7 lacks concrete dates or a specific scenario, turning into an abstract checklist.
observations.learnerCost: Beginners get an unhelpful circular explanation of effective service and a generic checklist instead of a concrete worked example to model.

observations.claim: In Lesson 2, the hook introduces Raimundo facing budget-limit cuts, but screen 2 jumps straight into final court judgments without connecting to the hook or using a concrete case, and screen 12 (ato motivado) is introduced right before the application without any check or application testing it.
observations.learnerCost: The abrupt jump breaks the lesson's opening story and leaves the motivated-act requirement unpracticed.

observations.claim: Lesson 2's application asks which of proposal A (administrative process for misconduct) and proposal B (budget-limit dismissal) does not depend on a court ruling, even though neither route requires a judicial sentence under the Constitution.
observations.learnerCost: This flawed prompt can mislead the writer and learner into thinking budget-limit dismissals require a court decision, or make the question ambiguous.

location.detail: Pedir qual não depende de sentença judicial e o que impede a outra: A pode seguir pela via administrativa; B ainda não cumpriu as medidas prévias.

observations.claim: Sets visualKind to table on Lesson 2's application even though proposals A and B describe two different narrative routes (misconduct process vs. spending-limit cuts) without parallel columns.
observations.learnerCost: Forces two non-parallel cases into an awkward table that adds layout clutter without aiding comparison.

observations.claim: Uses dense, legalistic phrasing for a beginner level ('exercício funcional contado para essa finalidade', 'sentença ainda recorrível não satisfaz essa hipótese', 'disciplinada apenas por portaria') and sticks to generic 'órgão' and 'setor de pessoal' rather than concrete Brazilian public institutions such as a prefeitura, secretaria, or órgão federal.
observations.learnerCost: Beginners have to wade through stiffer legal language and less recognizable Brazilian public-sector contexts.

overall.reason: A gives the writer a clearer, better-sequenced beginner plan with concrete Brazilian public-sector cases, plain explanations of legal terms, and solid worked examples, while B has a major flaw in Lesson 2's application prompt along with circular wording, an abrupt transition in Lesson 2, and stiffer legal phrasing.

criteria.reason: Both outputs have the exact same single-lesson scope, title, description, can-do line, and skill definition.

A opens with an everyday bakery scene ending on the lesson's question and builds concrete-to-name explanations that connect smoothly to the guess on screen 3. B replaces the hook with an abstract classification and formula, leaves screen 3 referring to an unintroduced bakery, and gives pure textbook definitions with no concrete cases on screens 2 and 4.
Both plans use the exact same categorize activity on screen 8 and keep all other screens text-only with no unnecessary visuals.

A stays in plain, everyday Brazilian Portuguese suited to beginners throughout. B opens with an unexplained algebraic formula (CT = CF + CVu · q) and academic accounting jargon ('faixa relevante', 'nível de atividade', 'custo variável unitário') that does not fit a beginner audience.

observations.claim: The opening hook (screen 1) is an abstract cost classification with an algebraic formula instead of an everyday scene ending on a question, which also leaves screen 3 ('Se a confeitaria passar um mês sem produzir...') referring to a bakery that was never introduced.
observations.learnerCost: Learners start with a dry formula instead of a relatable moment, then hit a confusing reference to an unintroduced bakery on screen 3.

location.detail: Apresente a classificação dos custos segundo seu comportamento em relação ao volume de atividade: custos fixos (CF) e custos variáveis (CV), com CT = CF + CVu · q.

observations.claim: The first two explanations (screens 2 and 4) give abstract textbook definitions without any concrete case or everyday example, and screen 4 does not connect back to the rent guess on screen 3.
observations.learnerCost: The writer receives abstract definitions instead of concrete-to-name teaching briefs, making it harder for a beginner to picture how fixed and variable costs work.

observations.claim: For a beginner lesson, screens 1, 2, and 4 introduce an unnecessary algebraic formula (CT = CF + CVu · q) before any intuition and rely on technical accounting terms ('faixa relevante', 'nível de atividade', 'custo variável unitário (CVu)', 'montante total') instead of everyday words.
observations.learnerCost: A beginner learning to manage a small business is likely to feel lost or intimidated right at the start of the lesson.

overall.reason: A provides a cohesive, concrete, beginner-friendly plan from start to finish, whereas B breaks the opening hook, introduces an unmotivated algebraic formula and heavy accounting jargon on screens 1, 2, and 4, and leaves screen 3 pointing to a bakery that was never introduced.
